top_story: New scrutiny of the April strike that killed seven World Central Kitchen staff on the road to Rafah sharpens evidence that Israeli forces hit a deconflicted aid convoy after a food delivery mission they had helped coordinate, reinforcing concerns that expansive targeting practices in Gaza are collapsing the distinction between militants and protected civilians. The significance extends beyond the single attack: it deepens humanitarian paralysis, deters international relief operations, and leaves displaced Palestinians facing even tighter constraints on food access and movement. In Iran, the reported torture and threatened execution of twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi shows a parallel logic of coercion, where the state uses extreme violence to punish protest-linked dissent and force compliance through fear. Together these cases point to a regional pattern in which security institutions treat civilian protection as subordinate to deterrence, with lasting costs for public trust, civic space, and basic survival.
